answer: Yes. The subtext enriches the story rather than feeling forced. The empty flat suggests an unrealized life and Daniel’s lingering attachment to his former self, while Isabel’s careful silences reveal vulnerability and emotional generosity beneath their ordinary conversations. The recurring keys, rooms, and boats connect these emotions to the physical setting. Finally, “Every year” becomes less a literal commitment than an offering of renewed intimacy, giving the ending resonance beyond the canoe trip itself.
